name: Bai Ji Guan
parentage: One of the four original, legendary Wuyi cultivars, named for its unique appearance.
description: 'White Cockscomb'. A rare and unique member of the 'Si Da Ming Cong', Bai Ji Guan stands apart from all other Wuyi oolongs. It is named for its peculiar pale, yellowish-green leaves and is processed with a much lighter hand, resulting in a creamy, sweet, and custardy flavor profile that contrasts sharply with the dark, roasty character of its famous brethren.
plantType: Small, slow-growing, semi-upright bush with delicate branches (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Requires a specific microclimate within the Wuyi Mountains. It is less hardy than other Yancha cultivars and requires great care.
processing: Processing Bai Ji Guan requires immense skill and a light touch. The leaves are more fragile than other Wuyi cultivars, so the bruising and oxidation steps must be gentle to avoid bitterness and preserve its delicate aromatics.
oxidation: Oxidation is kept very light for a Yancha (20-30%). This preserves the leaf's natural pale color and its sweet, creamy, and corn-like flavor notes.
roasting: Roasting is minimal and done at a very low temperature. It is more of a final drying bake than a flavor-altering roast. The goal is to stabilize the tea while allowing its inherent sweetness and unique flavor to shine.
versatility: Extremely specialized. Bai Ji Guan represents a unique, almost historical style of light Yancha. It is not versatile and can only be made in this specific way.

china: Fujian Province (Wuyi Mountains - very small production area)

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha - Light Style).Bai Ji Guan Yancha: Its only expression is a lightly oxidized and lightly roasted oolong, a style designed to preserve its delicate, sweet, and creamy nature.

sensory.aroma: Delicate floral notes, sweet corn, cream, buttery pastry
sensory.flavor: Custardy, sweet, with notes of yellow summer fruits (like pawpaw or melon) and a subtle mineral finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Creamy, smooth, and surprisingly thick with very low astringency. The liquor is a pale, bright golden-yellow.
